member.name: T:Mfr.Filters.Formatting.Tokens.Meta.SubstringToken
member.summary: Resolves the <substr:…> token (substring over resolved source text).

remarks.para: Named arguments (order-independent), for example <substr:start=1, end=5, source=<file-name>>. Whitespace around = and commas is ignored. Commas inside balanced <…> belong to nested templates, not to option boundaries.
Positions are 1-based. Negative positions count from the right: -1 is the last character, -2 is the second-to-last, and so on. Out-of-range positions are clamped to the nearest valid boundary.

When the resolved start position is less than or equal to the resolved end position, the characters at positions [start, end] (inclusive) are returned. When the resolved start exceeds the resolved end (crossed arguments), the characters at positions (end, start] are returned — the range between them, exclusive of end and inclusive of start.
source may be a nested format token such as <full-name> or a literal with embedded tokens; it is resolved before the substring is applied.

member.name: M:Mfr.Filters.Replace.ReplaceListParser.ParseFile(System.String)
member.summary: Parses and validates replace-list entries from a file.
member.remarks:
Expected format:
Comment lines may appear anywhere and must start with //, \\, or # (hash followed by a space, after optional leading whitespace).
Empty lines are ignored.
Each replace entry is two lines: search line starting with S: and replacement line starting with R:.
Search and replacement lines cannot be empty (excluding the prefix). Use <EMPTY> on replacement lines to strip the matched search text.
Search and replacement lines must be at most the configured list-file line limit (default 1000 characters each).
At least one replacement entry must be present.
Example file content:
# START OF REPLACE LIST S:a R:b
S:. R:_ # END OF REPLACE LIST
member.param: Replace-list file path.
member.returns: Parsed replace-list entries in file order.
